[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick round of intros — ill kick it off, maya from redwood, lucas our se and priya on cs.
[00:07] Daniel: hi, daniel here, we'll be running the pilot, sofia is our eng lead, tom handles security, kira is our sres.
[00:16] Lucas: great, um quick agenda, renewal numbers, pilot scope, perf benchmarks, and security checklist.
[00:23] Sofia: our execs want a simple ask — predictability and residency. we need EU-hosted or onprem option for PHI-ish workloads, timeline is quarter end jan feb is tight.
[00:35] Maya: yes totally. regarding the retainer, we proposed a 10% uplift to cover burst capacity and dedicated pool reservation. that was in the renewal sheet i shared.
[00:45] Tom: can you walk through what "dedicated" means here? like is it VPC, VPC peering, or onprem? and kms key access?
[00:54] Lucas: good question. dedicated in our model means reserved capacity in our dedicated fleet with VPC peering option; for onprem we do a private deployment where control plane is customer-managed then we integrate KMS or HSM depending on policy. note — sometimes the transcript engine says VPCV or VP C which is noisy.
[01:12] Kira: latency is a hard constraint for us — p95 under 120ms for most 256 token calls, anything above that will impact user flows. we plan to run synthetic traffic from eu-west nodes.
[01:23] Lucas: understood. we typically see p95 ~80-150ms depending on model and quant, but for private onprem setups we can get consistent sub-120ms with tuning (batching disabled for single token low-latency path, kv cache warmup). we'll run a baseline with your payload.
[01:40] Daniel: the pricing change — 10% sounds reasonable but need to see the math on the per-token delta and committed throughput. also, what's the fallback if the pilot doesn't meet latency?
[01:50] Maya: fallback — we can provision EU-hosted dedicated capacity as interim; also routing policies can failover to a higher tier region. we'll outline SLA and fallbacks in the SOW.
[01:58] Sofia: SOC2 and data residency — tom will need our legal/security review, can you provide the attestation and what logs you keep?
[02:07] Priya: yes we'll send SOC2 report, ISO statement and the audit log retention options. we also have an audit trail for token-level access and per-route traces in the console.
[02:18] Tom: about KMS: we need customer-managed keys (BYOK) and want to know whether Redwood stores any unencrypted secrets; also can we bring our HSM?
[02:27] Lucas: we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and customers can bring HSM for onprem. Redwood doesn't persist plaintext model inputs after processing in hosted flows; for private deployments encryption-in-transit and at-rest with your keys is default. small caveat — function names or some metadata may appear in logs but we can scrub those, will note as a config.
[02:45] Daniel: timeline — if we sign renewal by 12/12 can we start pilot mid-December?
[02:52] Maya: yes — priya will coordinate calendar, but we need the security checklist and kickoff attendee list to finalize.
[03:00] Lucas: i'll need a sample prompt set and a small sandbox data set for the perf run; 1k requests at different concurrency points is enough. prefer to mirror your prod 95th percentile pattern.
[03:12] Sofia: we'll provide a representative prompt set, it's mostly multi-turn clinical triage flows with short context windows ~200 tokens.
[03:20] Kira: question — what about model variants? do you fall back to a smaller quantized model that might be cheaper but slightly different quality? how do we guard against quality regressions in auto-failover?
[03:31] Lucas: good — we have model variant routing policies that prefer the primary model and only fall back to compatibles; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles and can run evals on holdout prompt sets to detect regressions — we'll include a quality gate in the pilot to block auto-failover until you approve.
[03:50] Tom: also can you show how traces map back to tokens? we have concerns about PII leakage in logs.
[03:56] Priya: we can toggle token-level obfuscation, and our console shows redacted traces for regulated customers; we'll include a readout doc.
[04:05] Daniel: ok sounds good. competitor question — we've been trialing BigCloudAI's managed endpoints; they promise lower cost but had inconsistent latency in eu. why pick Redwood?
[04:15] Maya: two reasons: production predictability (batching, KV cache, routing) and unified interface across hosted and private so you don't re-arch for sovereignty. also our latency/throughput telemetry is token-granular for billing transparency.
[04:29] Sofia: pricing transparency will matter, and can we get a P&L run for the next 12 months if we take the uplift?
[04:35] Maya: yes we'll share a cost model with assumptions — monthly commit, unit token cost, expected cache hit rates.
[04:42] Lucas: technical note — for the EU onprem pilot we'll provision a staging VM set with our runtime; you can bring your own GPU or we can supply. on the runtime side, sequence length distribution matters for kernel selection and perf.
[04:56] Kira: ops question — how's the failover tested? do you do automated canary rollouts? we can't have silent regressions during peak.
[05:05] Lucas: yes canary and A/B rollouts are supported; we can schedule traffic mirroring and have automatic rollback policies tied to latency/error budgets.
[05:14] Maya: let's recap: Redwood to update SOW with 10% uplift, include pilot terms; SE to run perf tests; Security to get SOC2/ISO and KMS docs; CSM to schedule kickoff.
[05:26] Daniel: agreed — i'll get internal stakeholders aligned and share the approval path.
[05:31] Tom: i'll send over the compliance checklist and KMS parity requirements.
[05:36] Priya: we'll send calendar invite for pilot kickoff and the renewal quote by end of week.
[05:40] Maya: any other blockers?
[05:43] Sofia: not from eng; just need results from the benchmark.
[05:47] Kira: same — security sign-off after docs review.
[05:50] Maya: okay thanks everyone, we'll follow-up in the thread, and lucas will ping the perf doc.
